issues.description: O(N²) parsing complexity due to string slicing. any-char and satisfy use substring to consume a single character, which involves copying the remainder of the string in most Scheme implementations.
issues.code_snippet:
(let* ([ch (string-ref input 0)]
       [rest (substring input 1 (string-length input))]
       [new-pos (advance-pos (state-pos state) ch)]
       [new-state (make-state rest new-pos)])
issues.suggested_fix: Change the Parser State to use an integer offset into the original string instead of passing substrings. This will make character consumption O(1).

issues.description: O(N²) algorithm for list shuffling. random-shuffle-eff uses list-ref and list-set inside a loop, both of which are O(N) operations on linked lists.
issues.code_snippet:
(letrec ([shuffle-step
          (lambda (i current-list)
                  (if (>= i (- n 1))
                      (eff-return current-list)
                      (eff-bind (random-int-eff i (- n 1))
                                (lambda (j)
                                        (shuffle-step (+ i 1)
                                                      (list-swap current-list i j))))))])
issues.suggested_fix: Convert the list to a vector, perform an in-place Fisher-Yates shuffle (which is O(N)), and then convert back to a list.

issues.description: Inefficient epsilon-closure calculation. The use of 'member' on the 'visited' list makes the algorithm O(S²) where S is the number of states.
issues.code_snippet:
(let loop ([frontier (list state)] [visited '()])
     (if (null? frontier)
         visited
         (let ([s (car frontier)])
              (if (member s visited)
                  (loop (cdr frontier) visited)
issues.suggested_fix: Use a hash table or a bitset for the 'visited' set to achieve O(1) lookup and O(S) total complexity for the closure.

issues.description: O(N*M) complexity for set union operation. Using 'exists' inside 'fold-left' over lists leads to quadratic behavior for set operations used heavily in subset construction.
issues.code_snippet:
(define (union eq? xs ys)
  (fold-left (lambda (acc x)
                     (if (exists (lambda (y) (eq? x y)) acc) acc (cons x acc)))
             ys xs))
issues.suggested_fix: Use a more efficient set representation like a hash set or a sorted list (allowing O(N) union).

issues.description: Inefficient string construction for state names. Using 'string-append' in a 'fold-left' loop results in O(N²) complexity for name generation because strings are copied on every append.
issues.code_snippet:
(fold-left (lambda (acc s)
                   (if (string=? acc "")
                       (symbol->string s)
                       (string-append acc "," (symbol->string s))))
           ""
           (list-sort symbol<? states))
issues.suggested_fix: Use 'string-join' or an output string port to collect all symbols and join them once.

issues.description: O(N²) whitespace trimming in INI parser. The loop calls 'reverse' multiple times on the character list to check the last element.
issues.code_snippet:
(let loop ([chars chars])
     (if (or (null? chars)
             (not (char-whitespace? (car (reverse chars)))))
         (list->string chars)
         (loop (reverse (cdr (reverse chars))))))
issues.suggested_fix: Convert to string first and use a more efficient trimming function, or iterate once from the end of the list to find the first non-whitespace character.

issues.description: Excessive allocation in hot paths. make-pos allocates a new list and tag for every character consumed during parsing.
issues.code_snippet:
(define (make-pos line col offset)
  (list 'pos line col offset))
issues.suggested_fix: Use a record type or a more compact representation (like a raw vector or a single integer encoding all three values) to reduce GC pressure.

issues.description: Inefficient result collection in NonDet effect. Using 'apply append' on results from mapped recursive calls can lead to quadratic behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a tail-recursive accumulator or a difference list (nested lambdas) to collect results in O(N) time.

summary: Identified several critical O(N²) algorithms in core parsing and effect handling logic. Most significant issues are string slicing in the parser and linked-list operations in the random shuffle and FSM closure.
